taxonomic_note: Accepted in the current Kew/POWO Tradescantia backbone; learner retained at species rank.
look_here_first: Start with size and lower-stem hairiness. Giant spiderwort is the robust, usually single-stemmed member of this trio, reaching about 90 cm in the Williamson treatment; the lower stem is essentially glabrous while the upper internodes become finely hairy. Its conspicuous paired leaflike bracts and relatively broad strap-shaped leaves reinforce the ID.

project_inclusion.range_basis: Hays County wild occurrence documentation; UT Plant Resources Center Travis County herbarium index; UT Williamson County species treatment.
project_inclusion.range_guardrail: County PASS uses explicit Hays occurrence plus Travis/Williamson flora-herbarium records; no broad Central Texas range inference.

best_field_traits: robust perennial, usually 1-stemmed at the base
suberect habit to about 90 cm in the Williamson treatment
lower stems essentially glabrous; upper internodes puberulent to short-pilose
strap-shaped to narrowly lanceolate-linear leaves, to about 39 mm wide locally
terminal condensed cymes subtended by conspicuous leaflike bracts
morphology_keys.comparison_training: T. humilis is low, many-stemmed and conspicuously hairy. T. occidentalis is narrower-leaved and has obvious long-stalked glandular hairs on the internodes. T. gigantea is the taller robust plant with relatively smooth lower stems.
